title: Density-layer movement offsets part of the BATS column oxygen loss between 1989-1998 and 2016-2025
abstract: We test whether the BATS oxygen loss on density 26.5 also occurs in a fixed-depth column. We use BATS bottle data v10 and an exact symmetric split of epoch mean profiles into oxygen change at fixed density and density displacement. Between 1989-1998 and 2016-2025, the 200-800 m reference-density oxygen stock falls by 3.20 mol/m2 (95% two-year block interval: 2.15-4.21 mol/m2 of loss). The property term is -4.49 mol/m2 and displacement is +1.29 mol/m2, which offsets 29% of the property loss. The 100-1000 m layer loses 3.53 mol/m2, with a 37% offset. Both signs persist with a smaller bottle gap and with a joint change of endpoint years, month coverage and block length. Density-layer movement thus hides part of the loss rather than causing it. This is a coordinate decomposition at one site, not a causal ventilation or respiration budget. It does not establish the full-depth or basin inventory. Code, annual aggregates, source hashes, tests and figures permit reproduction.

display.caption: BATS oxygen change by depth and integrated layer. Density displacement offsets part of the loss at fixed density. Intervals use two-year blocks of years.
